key_insight: Instead of building equivariant diffusion architectures, canonicalize each sample to a unique pose/order (an orbit representative) and train a standard (non‑equivariant) diffusion model on those canonicalized data; invert the canonicalization at generation time to recover symmetry‑invariant outputs.
problem_solved: Avoids the complexity, computational cost, and engineering difficulty of designing and training equivariant/invariant generative models for data with group symmetries (e.g., permutation of graph nodes, 3D rotations of molecular structures).
method: Canonicalization: map each sample to a deterministic (or learned) canonical pose/order that represents its symmetry orbit (e.g., fix node ordering or align coordinates).
Diffusion training: train a standard, unconstrained diffusion denoiser on the canonicalized dataset instead of enforcing equivariance in the model architecture.
Reprojection: at generation time, sample in canonical space with the diffusion model and apply the inverse transform (or random symmetry) to produce symmetry‑correct outputs in original space.
impact: Provides a simpler, modular alternative to equivariant models that preserves symmetry in the generated distribution while reducing model complexity and engineering overhead—making high‑quality molecular and scientific generative modeling more accessible and scalable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input sample → canonicalizer → diffusion model → inverse transform → symmetric output.
Orbit illustration: set of symmetric variants (rotations/permutations) collapsing to a single canonical representative.
Comparison chart: model complexity/training cost vs. sample quality for equivariant vs. canonicalization-based diffusion.
Molecular examples: before/after canonicalization and generated 3D molecule renderings to show invariance preserved.
paper_title: Rethinking Diffusion Models with Symmetries through Canonicalization with Applications to Molecular Graph Generation
paper_authors: Cai Zhou, Zijie Chen, Zian Li, Jike Wang, Kaiyi Jiang
